Test Description: Validate that GPIO_8 to GPIO_27 registers power-on/reset to their documented default values (ignoring bit 0) and that writable fields accept data patterns while read-only fields retain their default values. Verify read/write behavior using write and read masks with multiple data patterns.
Meta Test Description: The test performs two phases: (1) Default value verification and (2) Write/Read verification. Phase 1 iterates i=0..CNT-1 over addr_array[i] and, if skip_rst_array[i]==1 or read_mask_array[i]==0, skips. Otherwise reads data_rd=read_reg(addr), masks out bit0 via data=(data_rd & 0xfffffffe), and compares against default_value_array[i]; increments def_fail_cnt on mismatch. Phase 2 iterates over six test patterns {0xffffffff,0xaaaaaaaa,0x55555555,0xf5f5f5f5,0xA5A5A5A5,0xffff0000}. For each pattern, it writes (data_wr & write_mask_array[i]) to each address where skip_array[i]==0 and write_mask_array[i]!=0. Then reads back data_rd=(read_reg(addr) & read_mask_array[i]) for each address where read_mask_array[i]!=0 and write_mask_array[i]!=0. It computes wr_n=(write_mask_array[i] ^ 0xffffffff) and expected value exp_val=((data_wr & read_mask_array[i] & write_mask_array[i]) | (wr_n & read_mask_array[i] & default_value_array[i])). If data_rd != exp_val, increments wr_fail_cnt. At end, the test calls finish(1) if (def_fail_cnt>0 || wr_fail_cnt>0) else finish(0). A soft reset check function is present but compiled out (#ifdef 0).
Remarks: Bit 0 is intentionally ignored during reset-value comparison for all targeted GPIO registers. Only GPIO_8 through GPIO_27 are targeted in this test iteration. Registers marked non-readable or non-writable by masks are skipped accordingly. The soft reset check is disabled in the current test build.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1. For each GPIO register from GPIO_8 to GPIO_27 that is readable and not marked as skipped for reset verification, read the register and compare its value (with bit 0 ignored) against its documented reset default value. 2. For each of the defined test data patterns, write the pattern to each GPIO register from GPIO_8 to GPIO_27 that is writable and not marked as skipped, applying the write mask to limit writes to writable bits. 3. Read back each affected GPIO register that is readable and writable, applying the read mask to the returned value. 4. For each readback, confirm that writable bits match the written pattern and that non-writable (read-only) bits remain at their reset default values. 5. Record any mismatches as failures and report overall test status as PASS only if no default-value or write/read mismatches are observed.

Test Description: Enable negative-edge interrupt on GPIO pads 8–39. For each pad, generate a single falling edge, verify that an interrupt is received, confirm the group status bit for the pad is set, then clear per-pad and group interrupt status and confirm they are cleared.
Meta Test Description: The test enables the GIC IRQ line for the targeted GPIO block (IRQ 87 or 88) and enables the system-level interrupt INTR_EN1 for the selected GPIO instance. It configures each per-pad GPIO register starting at GPIO_8 + (i*4) to set interrupt mode for negative-edge detection and to perform initial clearing (writing (1<<20)|(1<<18)|(1<<16)). Before each iteration, it clears per-pad raw status via gpio_intr_raw_stclr1 with a one-hot wr_val = (1<<i) and enables the group interrupt mask via INTR1_INTR_EN1 with wr_val. It sets int_pend = 1 and uses the stimulus register at 0xA0243FFC to first drive all pads high (0xFFFFFFFF), waits, then drives all except the target pad high (~wr_val), producing a falling edge on pad (i+8). It polls with a timeout for int_pend to be cleared by the ISR. In Default_IRQHandler, it sets int_pend = 0, re-drives the stimulus high (0xFFFFFFFF), reads per-pad config/status at GPIO_8 + (i*4), and checks: (rdata & 0x1) must be 0; (rdata & 0x2) must be non-zero indicating interrupt detection. It then reads group status INTR1_INTR_STS1 and verifies the one-hot bit is set; clears the per-pad interrupt by writing (1<<20)|(1<<16) to the per-pad register and writing to gpio_intr_raw_stclr1; re-reads INTR1_INTR_STS1 and expects 0. Finally, it clears system raw status via RAW_STCR1 and clears the GIC IRQ line. Any timeout or mismatch increments test_err. Test ends with finish(test_err).
Remarks: Requires GIC interrupt lines 87/88 to be enabled depending on the GPIO instance. Uses a stimulus register at 0xA0243FFC to toggle levels on pads 8–39. Group and per-pad interrupt enables must be set before generating edges. The test uses timeouts to avoid hangs if interrupts are not received.
Test Steps / Procedure: 1. Enable GIC IRQ for the target GPIO interrupt output and enable the system interrupt in INTR_EN1. 2. Configure GPIO pads 8–39 for negative-edge interrupt detection and clear any pending status. 3. For each pad from 8 to 39: a) Clear the pad’s raw interrupt status and enable its mask in INTR1_INTR_EN1. b) Arm pending flag and generate a falling edge on the pad using the stimulus register. c) Wait for the ISR to indicate interrupt reception within the timeout. 4. In ISR handling: a) Verify the per-pad status indicates an interrupt was detected. b) Verify the pad’s bit is set in INTR1_INTR_STS1. c) Clear per-pad raw status and confirm INTR1_INTR_STS1 is cleared. d) Clear system raw status and the GIC IRQ. 5. Report PASS only if all pads generate and clear interrupts correctly without timeouts or mismatches.

Test Description: Enable positive-edge interrupt across GPIO pads 8–39. Drive a rising edge and verify that an interrupt is received, the group interrupt status indicates activity, then clear per-pad raw status for all pads and confirm group status clears. Verify the system raw status is cleared and the interrupt line is deasserted.
Meta Test Description: The test enables GIC IRQ (87 or 88) and enables the system-level interrupt in INTR_EN1. It programs each per-pad register at GPIO_8 + (i*4) with 0x00020000 (bit17=1) to enable positive-edge detection. It configures GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP1..4 to 0x000000FF (input configuration). It enables all pad masks in INTR1_INTR_EN1 (0xFFFFFFFF). For each iteration, it drives the stimulus low (0x00000000), arms int_pend=1, then drives high (0xFFFFFFFF) to create a rising edge. It waits with a timeout for ISR to clear int_pend. It verifies INTR1_INTR_STS1 becomes 0. It then clears the system raw status via RAW_STCR1 and reads back to ensure the bit is cleared, re-enables INTR1_INTR_EN1 to 0xFFFFFFFF, and clears the GIC IRQ line. Any timeout or mismatch increments test_err. The test ends with finish(test_err).
Remarks: Requires GIC interrupt lines 87/88 to be enabled depending on the GPIO instance. Uses a stimulus register at 0xA0243FFC to toggle pads 8–39. All group masks are enabled; ISR masks group during service and re-enables afterward. GPIO I/O control groups 1–4 must be properly configured for input.
